q: What is the first step when building a VLSM addressing plan?
opts: Sort the networks from the most hosts to the fewest
Use the same mask for every network
explain: Allocating the largest networks first keeps every block aligned on its boundary and avoids overlaps.

q: What is the main benefit of VLSM?
opts: It conserves addresses by sizing each subnet to its need
It removes the need for a subnet mask
It makes every subnet the same size
explain: Variable-length masks let a 2-host link use a /30 while a 100-host LAN uses a /25, instead of wasting a large block on every network.

q: Which prefix is the usual choice for a point-to-point link between two routers?
explain: A /30 has 4 addresses: network, two usable hosts, and broadcast — exactly enough for two router interfaces.

q: A plan needs networks of 14, 100, and 30 hosts. In what order should they be allocated?
explain: Always allocate largest to smallest.
